original_test_intent: Prove that the second processor/HPM position is populated as the approved 2P HPM1 configuration, physically connected to BMC I2C-7, and independently reachable through the correct BMC controller and mux channel with all required HPM1 devices returning their expected identities.
original_method: Verify the platform is truly in the required 2P state and bind logical I2C-7 to the BMC controller, adapter, mux/channel and HPM1 connector; define the HPM1-specific 7-bit addresses and identity registers distinct from HPM0; have an operator inspect and photograph the HPM1/second-HPM connection under the service procedure; preserve bus logs; use only allowlisted read-only transactions on the mapped channel; demonstrate the complete HPM1 response set and absence of bus faults, stopping before any scan/write or retry that could disturb the live bus.
manual_activity: An operator verifies the second processor/HPM position is populated, checks HPM1 connector/cable seating under the vendor procedure and records target-bound photos.
required_inputs: Approved 2P population record and HPM1 versus HPM0 physical/topology distinction
Logical I2C-7 to BMC controller/adapter/mux/channel/HPM1 connector map
HPM1 expected device table with 7-bit addresses, safe identity registers/masks and values
Vendor-approved non-destructive read method, prohibited transactions, physical service and bus recovery procedure
safety_requirements: Use only the approved BMC/OOB path and mapped HPM1 channel
Do not accept HPM0 responses as HPM1 evidence; bind each response to the second-HPM mux path
Never quick-write, scan unknown devices, write EEPROM/control registers or service a live connector without approval
Stop on timeout, wrong-channel response, missing/unexpected device, stuck bus, arbitration/error storm or BMC instability
agent_execution_scope: Validate 2P population, HPM1 physical/path map, device oracle and transaction allowlist
After operator confirmation, collect read-only HPM1-bound identity and BMC bus-health evidence
Compare every expected second-HPM device and reject wrong-channel or first-HPM substitution
Do not guess adapter syntax, probe unknown addresses, alter wiring/device state, reset the bus/BMC or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the 2P state and exact I2C-7 controller/mux/channel/HPM1 connector map
Approve HPM1-specific addresses/registers/values, safe command list, error tolerance and physical/recovery procedure
Review physical plus software evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: i2cdetect/i2cget may support the check after mapping and safety approval, but `i2cdetect -y I2C-7` neither proves syntax nor distinguishes the HPM1 channel from HPM0.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the owner-approved BMC/vendor read-only method on the mapped I2C-7 HPM1 mux path and query only the second-HPM allowlist, retaining identity responses and bus-health state.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC I2C-7 to HPM1 second-HPM/2P scope, AI_VR_I2C_bus7 bundle, and 10/10-minute allocation remain; device map and adapter number are not invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: MEDIUM HPM1-SPECIFIC HYBRID PHYSICAL AND BMC I2C FUNCTIONAL CHECK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: First prove the 2P/HPM1 population and physical connector, then select the exact downstream mux channel and validate a second-HPM-specific read-only identity oracle plus clean bus health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds 2P-state proof, HPM0/HPM1 disambiguation, exact topology, safe identity reads, operator evidence and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A shared address pattern or scan on the wrong channel can look correct while HPM1 is absent or disconnected; a photo cannot prove BMC communication.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Live I2C devices can react to generic scans/reads, and incorrect mux selection can validate or disturb another HPM rather than the intended second path.

project_override_considerations: A vendor BMC inventory may substitute only if it identifies the exact HPM1 mux/channel and returns stable HPM1 device identities. HPM0 or host-I2C output is not equivalent 2P coverage.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, authorization and proof of the required 2P/HPM1 population
Timestamped HPM1 connector/path photos and physical inspection record
BMC controller/adapter/mux/channel/HPM1 map and second-HPM address/register/value allowlist
Exact approved commands plus complete HPM1 observed identity-response comparison
Pre/post BMC/I2C timeout/NACK/arbitration/stuck-bus logs and unchanged management state

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure, Criteria and bundle consistently target BMC I2C-7 to HPM1 in a 2P/second-HPM configuration.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The second-HPM physical and communication objective is clear. The 2P topology, device oracle, safe method and operator evidence are supplyable prerequisites.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2158 Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00045-V003: approve proof of the 2P/HPM1 population; logical BMC I2C-7 to controller/adapter/mux/channel/HPM1 connector map; HPM1-specific 7-bit device addresses and stable identity registers/values distinct from HPM0; vendor-approved non-destructive commands/prohibited transactions, physical photo procedure, bus-error acceptance, aborts, and recovery.

review_improvement: Makes second-HPM identity explicit so a first-HPM or wrong-mux response cannot falsely satisfy the 2P test, while protecting the live BMC bus.
independent_technical_reasoning: The engineering distinction in this row is not merely bus number: it is the second HPM present only in the approved 2P configuration. Repeated address layouts behind muxes make a raw scan ambiguous, so evidence must prove channel selection and device identity specific to HPM1. Physical population and logical reachability are complementary, and neither can replace the other. Read allowlisting avoids transactions that VRs or EEPROMs may interpret as state changes.
